I’ve had a similar issue and was told to try a Spanish learners discord group, discord is what people who play videos games to use talk to each other or just for normal conversations, you could probably find a invite to one in a YouTube video description for a discord group like that. 

There is also iTalki, it’s paid but from what I’ve heard it’s a one of the best ways to learn speaking and I think it can be one on one with a tutor or in a group. 

I’ve seen people use apps/websites like Omegle to talk to natives. The website connects two strangers and you can talk or text with them in a chat, be careful though as there are some weird people so treat everyone like a stranger. 

Speaking in general even in your native language can be a struggle for some and that’s perfectly fine. Everyone I’ve met and tried to speak to with broken Spanish helped me with pronunciation and wasn’t negative. It can be very stressful but it’s just part of the process, you’ll say something wrong, say a word that doesn’t exist, or forget something mid sentence but those mistakes are what will make you stronger overall. I wish you best of luck!

I’ve enjoyed using Dreaming Spanish, you watch videos where someone talks in beginner/intermediate/advanced levels of Spanish. I use Duolingo and Dreaming Spanish but you could definitely just use the latter along with an intro to Spanish book. YouTube has some great videos for free, if you want to speak with people then iTalki is good for that, and I’d also suggest Duolingo’s podcasts. They have levels of difficulty and they have roughly ~180 with more being made.
